Absolutely. I eat meat regularly, but I understand the harsh treatment some farms practice on their livestock. If I can I try to get responsibly-grown meat, but it's not always possible. If kill-free meat became more available and was just as delicious, you bet your ass I'd go out of my way to get it even if it were a little more expensive.

Actually US meat is treated very humanely. The plants are regulated down to the number on slips to the number of vocalizations (and many more minute details). Also, if abuse DOES occur, it produces inferior meat (PSE and DFD). PSE was discarded upon inspection. The farmer and the plant LOSE MONEY if they mistreat animals. Even if the meat doesn't turn into PSE or DFD, stressed animals lose weight. Less weight, less money.

People just don't know WHY things are done. There are specific reasons for things, usually to prevent injury to the animal or handlers.

People watch an animal rights video, and assume all animals are treated the way they are in the video. The clips are either deceptive, old, show practices that aren't explained and if they were, would be acceptable, or use video from non-US plants.

I worked in a pork kill floor and a beef processing plant and grew up on a farm. I saw about a dozen instances of true abuse in 15 years. All were immediately fired, and several faced abuse charges and were convicted.

The truth is, all US animals are treated humanely.
